HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Low wide from the valley floor at the first grey of dawn. ONE device: one huge dark boulder rising as a pyramid in the centre of the frame against a pale fog sky. On its summit a Baekje general in yellow-cloth lamellar and a plumed helm, bow at full draw with his last arrow, an empty quiver on his hip, arrows stuck in the snow all round the rock. Halfway up the rock face Alchun climbs bare-handed, no weapon, looking up at him and grinning, an arrow-tear in his sleeve. At the foot of the rock, small and dark, Bidam stands back with his arms folded and his sword sheathed, clean. Behind, the long ragged line of Silla spearmen stopped at the valley lip, tiny in the fog. Cold dawn key from one side, long shadows on the snow. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = alchun, SECOND face = bidam. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_jade_gate_valley (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). ALCHUN Colour #8fb3e0. BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: His signature hybrid coat: a long white outer robe whose wide sleeves are embroidered with galloping black horses, with deep navy #141C2E bands down the lapels and a navy yoke across the shoulders, over a plum-magenta inner robe and dark sash; the bead string looped on the right wrist. Navy lives only in those lapel and shoulder bands and on the beads — never a glow. Colour #141C2E. PLACE Jade Gate Valley (옥문곡 (여근곡)) — attached board /pl_jade_gate_valley.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
